atoms.reason: Unanimous (A/B/C) and the correct foundational pattern: a dedicated capture thread feeding a ring buffer decouples recording FPS from YOLO/VLM load, which is the root cause being addressed. High impact and risk reduction. Simplicity is the only weak point (threads + buffer add complexity) and reversibility is low, but the architectural payoff justifies it.

Highly specific and technically sound: H.264 MP4 with PTS-derived CFR and +faststart is standard best practice for playable, streamable incident clips. Concrete, testable targets (8-12s, >=25 FPS). Backed by A and B; medium cost is reasonable for the deliverable quality it guarantees.

Best-scoring atom: archive-before-deliver establishes a durable source of truth independent of fragile Telegram delivery. Unanimous, trivially cheap, fully reversible, highly specific path, and strong risk reduction against data loss. Near-zero downside.

sendVideo is the correct API to produce an inline video, and graceful degradation to sendPhoto/text guarantees the alert still reaches operators when upload fails. Unanimous, high risk reduction. The only minor cost is the added fallback branching, slightly lowering simplicity.

Sampling VLM at exactly 1 FPS from the shared/ring buffer (rather than letting VLM gate decode) cleanly enforces the capture/analysis decoupling and bounds VLM cost. Unanimous and specific. Depends on DA-001's buffer existing, but consistent with it.

penalties.reason: Partial overlap/redundancy with DA-001 decoupling; offers several alternative fallback mechanisms without committing to one, and dynamic mid-flight capture switching is hard to implement safely.

atoms.reason: The resilience goal is sound and unanimous, but if DA-001 already isolates the recorder from analytics load, a watchdog that switches capture mechanisms mid-stream is partly redundant and adds significant complexity (high cost, low simplicity). Modify: keep the FPS watchdog/alerting but commit to a single fallback path (e.g., camera sub-stream or ffmpeg stream-copy) with defined switch hysteresis rather than an open menu.

Correct: OpenCV VideoWriter is notoriously unstable for timestamps/CFR, so preferring FFmpeg/GStreamer (with optional NVENC/VAAPI and a software fallback) materially improves encoding robustness. Unanimous. Slightly lower specificity because it lists multiple encoder options rather than fixing one, and adds an external dependency.

A cheap, high-value validation gate: ffprobe checks on existence, duration, FPS, and container integrity prevent shipping broken clips to operators. Unanimous, low cost, fully reversible, very specific thresholds. Pairs naturally with DA-003 and DA-002.

Exposing video_mp4, vlm_result, and telegram_message_id/status improves incident traceability and observability. Specific and feasible (A/B), but it is a reporting enhancement rather than core to the recording fix, so impact and risk reduction are moderate.

Offloading encode/upload to an async worker keeps the real-time detection/decision/alert loop responsive and lets alerts fire even when video processing lags or fails — correct and high impact (B/C). Cost is high and it lowers simplicity (queue infra, low reversibility), but it complements DA-001 rather than duplicating it.

penalties.reason: Single-proposal support (B only) and risks premature optimization: the JPEG-frames vs rolling-FFmpeg-segments choice should be driven by measured memory, not pre-committed.

atoms.reason: The principle is right — never buffer raw frames for pre-roll; impose a hard memory/disk cap with eviction. But it is the weakest-supported atom (B only), high cost, and prescribes a specific mechanism prematurely. Modify: adopt the bounded-buffer + cap requirement, but select JPEG-encoded frames vs rolling FFmpeg segments after profiling the actual pre-roll memory footprint.
